oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML brokered login should complete and yield a valid userinfo identity; otherwise the test setup is broken.
ZITADEL accepted a SAML assertion without AudienceRestriction, granting authorization to a client without upstream audience intent.

finding.sequence_description: Token exchange scope escalation: start with a limited-scope OIDC code flow (openid email), then attempt RFC8693 token exchange requesting expanded scopes (openid profile). Expect invalid_scope or returned scope not to include profile.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Scope-escalating token exchange succeeded (returned openid email profile) despite the prerequisite limited-scope code flow failing to mint a subject token, suggesting the exchange may not be bound to the intended upstream authorization context.

finding.sequence_description: Token exchange should validate subject_token audience: obtain a subject access token, then attempt token_exchange requesting an audience that is not in the subject token's audience set (using a reserved project audience scope to try to widen). Expect rejection (invalid_target/invalid_request) or no audience widening.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange succeeded even though the prerequisite subject access token was never minted (code exchange failed), indicating the exchange may not be bound to the intended subject_token/audience test setup (possible flow coherence / authorization-binding test invalidation).

sequence.description: Token exchange should enforce that the subject_token is intended for the requesting client. Obtain an access token via SAML-brokered OIDC for client_id, then attempt RFC8693 token_exchange using the same client credentials but requesting a different audience (project_id). If ZITADEL ignores subject_token audience constraints when the exchanging client is the same as the original, it may mint a token for an audience not covered by the upstream intent.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not mint tokens for audiences outside UpstreamIntent(subject_token) ∩ BrokerPolicy. Even if the exchanging client is the same, requested audience must be constrained by the subject_token's audience set.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control access token should be active and introspectable by the client in its audience; otherwise the test setup is invalid for I5 conclusions.
Token exchange accepted a subject_token and minted a token for audience=project_id, potentially exceeding the subject_token's upstream audience intent (audience binding bypass).
